doc.title: John Abercrombie interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001

title: Django Reinhardt
summary: Django: passion, fire and brilliance, and jazz despite not being American tradition.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Passion. Fire. Brilliance. Absolutely just brilliant. There is no other word for it. I mean just how anybody could play that way. Again I mean even when I went to school there was this criticism that Django is not really a jazz player. He had so much of the gypsy fire and the certain kind of scaler thing that he would do and just the way he would play, he didn’t sound like Charlie Christian. But to me it was still jazz. And I think that was one of the early experiences of hearing someone play who wasn’t coming from the American jazz tradition but who was improvising this incredible stuff and playing standard songs that everybody played all around the world. But he had his own way of playing them. So he was unique. I mean passionate, fiery, brilliant, unique. And he did it all with just two fingers or something. It’s pretty amazing.
